about: The language capability audit (MS12). Every campaign puzzle names one family in its reference spec; a blocked family or mode is refused by the content validator. Update this file when the language or the product gains a capability, never to let a puzzle through.

control_flow.note: IF / ELSE, WHILE, FOR, REMAINDER, FLOOR DIVIDE and running values on plain numbers, no list needed (Foundations, MS15).

array_scan.note: Lists: GET ELEMENT / SET ELEMENT / LENGTH / APPEND / REMOVE / SWAP, FOR, FOR EACH, WHILE.

prefix_sum.note: Running totals in a list built with APPEND.

hash_map.note: Maps with number, text or yes/no keys; a lookup may be NOTHING and is checked with IS NOTHING (L1).

hash_set.note: Sets of numbers, text or yes/no.

sliding_window.note: Index variables, running totals, maps for counts.

monotonic_deque.note: There are no deque blocks; a list with a moving head index stands in for one.

linked_list_traversal.note: NEXT NODE with IS NOT NOTHING narrowing (L1).

linked_list_relink.note: SET NEXT through a checked node; a program can re-link but never create a node.

linked_list_build.note: No block creates a list node.

tree_traversal.note: LEFT / RIGHT with narrowing, walked with a stack or a queue of nodes; no recursion.

tree_build.note: No block creates a tree node or sets a child.

graph_bfs.note: NEIGHBORS, NODE COUNT, MARK / VISITED, queues.

topological_order.note: In-degree counts in a list and a queue (Kahn).

weighted_shortest_path.note: Graphs carry no edge weights and there is no priority queue.

dp_iterative.note: Tables in lists, filled in order.

dp_grid.note: Lists of lists as input; rows read with GET ELEMENT twice.

recursion.note: Player functions that CALL themselves (L2): a FUNCTION per puzzle, each call with its own variables, depth counted against maxDepth.

backtracking.note: Recursion that tries a choice, CALLs itself, then undoes it (APPEND / REMOVE AT on a list passed by reference) (L2).

heap.note: No heap or priority-queue blocks, runtime value or fixture form.

sorting_builtin.note: There is no sort block; puzzles give sorted input when order matters.

strings.note: No text operations, and the editor cannot enter text.

pairs_tuples.note: The pair type has no blocks or fixture form; parallel lists stand in.

budget.note: A correct answer inside a deterministic operation budget (MS10).

optimize.note: Beat a correct-but-slow baseline by a declared factor (performance.baselineFactor).

restricted.note: Scarce memory cells, blocks or palette.

edge.note: The difficulty is in the edge cases the hidden tests hold.

complete.note: Needs a starter program: the schema and the editor have none yet.

repair.note: Needs a starter (buggy) program: the schema and the editor have none yet.

structure.note: Choosing a data structure among given skeletons needs a starter program.

trace.note: Needs a step-through view of a given program; there is no player trace UI.

predict.note: Needs a given program and an answer input; there is no predict UI.

complexity.note: The game never claims a complexity class; budgets stand in (MS10).

ops.note: Counting operations of a given program needs a starter program and an answer input.
